claims.text: It sent 880 model-generated, model-graded reports to a curated set of about 114 projects in 11 days, with scanning still incomplete [^5,6].

Punit Shah of Anthropic's Frontier Red Team posted on 2026-10-19 that "~650 projects applied", "114 accepted", and "77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings reported", with the parenthetical "we haven't scanned all projects yet" [^5].

Two hours later the @ClaudeDevs account repeated the totals: "The first scans have already reported 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings to maintainers," adding that scanning was continuing on more projects [^6].
The launch post describes the reports as "fully model-generated, without human review or triage," produced by "our strongest models (including Claude Mythos)" [^1].
OSS Scanner launched on 2026-10-08 and the totals were posted on 2026-10-19, so the window is 11 days, not 7 [^1,5].
The post containing the words "model-rated" drew about 70K, and Shah's own post about 25K [^5,7].
By our arithmetic, 880 reports across 114 accepted projects is about 7.7 per accepted project [^5].
Critical findings are 77 of 880, or 8.75%; the other 91.25% are labelled High [^5].
The repository had 845 enrollment PRs in total. 468 were closed without merging, about 233 were still open and 144 were merged, as of 2026-10-20 [^4].
Three projects often cited in the AI-bug-report debate are not in `projects/`: curl, PostgreSQL and the Linux kernel [^4].
Anthropic says outside pentesters checked "97 critical and high-severity vulnerabilities from the scanner across 48 projects", and that "85 (88%) met the bar for our CVD process" [^1].
By ARA arithmetic on the [^1] figures, 85/97 is 87.6%, with a Wilson 95% confidence interval of about 79.6% to 92.8%.
The duplicate share is 11/97 = 11.3% (CI ≈ 6.4%–19.2%) by our arithmetic [^1].
The single best maintainer datapoint is wolfSSL: "of the 74 reports we received, all but two were valid, and five became CVEs" [^1].
As of 2026-10-02 it lists 29,439 candidates, of which 6,123 were reviewed by external security firms and 5,674 confirmed valid [^9].
OSS Scanner's first-week reports are, by design, in the unreviewed category: Anthropic describes them as "fully model-generated, without human review or triage" [^2].
At the Mythos launch, contractors agreed exactly with Claude's severity in 89% of 198 manually reviewed reports [^11].
curl's confirmed-report rate, which had collapsed below 5% in 2025 [^21], was back to about 15–16% by April 2026, when Stenberg wrote "The slop situation is not a problem anymore" [^20].
Mythos called 8 of them Critical; "One of the eight Critical ratings held" [^13].
Fourteen of the 27 ratings disagreed, 13 of them overstated and one understated (jq) [^13].
Temporal received a Mythos Critical that maintainers scored 2.3, Low; MinIO went from Critical (model) to High (external firm) to Medium (maintainer) [^13].
Among findings that carried both a Claude rating and a maintainer rating, Claude called 91.5% critical or high, against 51.3% for the maintainers [^14].
Across all 2024 NVD CVEs, 47.2% were High or Critical (13.7% Critical, 33.5% High) [^47].
Anthropic's CVD dashboard reports, as of 2026-10-02, "83.0% exact agreement, 97.1% within one band" between Claude and external security firms over 1,337 findings [^9].
Only about 6% of published CVEs are ever seen exploited [^50], and CISA's KEV catalog lists 1,748 entries as of 2026-10-20 [^49].

Lead developer Daniel Stenberg wrote that the issue was "found and reported by Luna Tong at Anthropic using their new OSS Scanner", that "the report and the reproducible are awesome", and that it is "one of the worst vulnerabilities in curl in a long time" [^17].

Getting from the use-after-free to code execution needs the exact build, architecture, allocator and heap layout, plus an upload of about 135 KB, after which the attacker gets a command of roughly 23 bytes [^17].
Before October 2026, curl's most recent High CVE dated from October 2023 [^18], and by our tally of its security table only about 18% of its 239 CVEs are High or Critical (41 High, 2 Critical) [^26].
Punit Shah describes the curl find as the work of "an early version of OSS Scanner" [^5].
{label: Aisle Research, value: "25 CVEs", pct: 100}
Anthropic's two, CVE-2026-92392 and one Low, come to about 6% by our arithmetic [^25].
In May 2026, reviewing a Mythos scan of curl run by a third party, he found that five "confirmed" vulnerabilities came down to one Low CVE: three were false positives and one was "just a bug".
Readers should know that Wheeler works at OpenSSF, which receives Anthropic money through the Linux Foundation: $2.5M of Glasswing donations went to Alpha-Omega/OpenSSF [^52,33].
About a week after enrolling, its maintainer received "a report with 36 bugs, including 6 security vulnerabilities: 2 critical, 3 high, and 1 moderate," some of them more than four years old[^30].
One resulting pion/dtls advisory is rated Critical at CVSS 9.1 and credits "Anthropic's OSS Scanner"[^31].
The maintainer reviewed the bundle manually "one by one" and spent the whole day on it, because "Both Claude and Codex refused to help verify, triage, or develop proof-of-concept reproductions"[^30].

On 2026-10-20 Stenberg said that from October 26, LOW and MEDIUM reports go to public GitHub issues instead of the private security channel, since more than 90% of submissions are assessed below HIGH[^19].
The same dashboard counts 6,157 findings reported across 591 projects, 5,103 acknowledged by maintainers, and 516 patched upstream [^9].
By our arithmetic, 78% of disclosed findings therefore reached maintainers with no outside human check [^9].
VulnCheck's audit of Anthropic's public ledger found 202 fixes across 113 projects, against the 421 fixes the dashboard claimed at the time [^14].
DARPA's AIxCC finalists found 54 of 63 synthetic vulnerabilities and patched 43, and patched 11 of the 18 real zero-days they found, at an average of about 45 minutes and roughly $152 per task [^38].
Its key design choice is that ClusterFuzz files bugs automatically and also verifies fixes automatically, with disclosure at the verified fix or at 90 days [^37].
Its ClusterFuzz backend files them automatically, verifies fixes automatically, and discloses at the verified fix or after 90 days [^37].
Google credits it with helping identify and fix over 13,000 vulnerabilities and 50,000 bugs across 1,000 projects as of May 2025 [^36].
By our arithmetic, 2026's 81,927 records through 2026-10-19 already exceed all of 2025 by 71% [^39].
NIST reported that submissions grew 263% from 2020 to 2025, and it moved CVEs backlogged before 2026-03-01 to a "Not Scheduled" status [^40].
Of XBOW's roughly 1,060 HackerOne submissions, 208 were closed as duplicates and 209 as informative, about 39% by our arithmetic, while 130 were resolved [^44].
By our arithmetic, the 95% interval on 1-in-8 runs from about 2% to 47%, so the honest range for surviving criticals is roughly 2 to 36 of 77, not "about 10" [^5,13].
Applied to the 880, that ratio would suggest roughly 493 findings that maintainers would call critical or high, by our arithmetic [^14,5].
Elastic received more than 1,390 bug-bounty reports in H1 2026, against a historical 600–850 a year, and rejected about 70% at analysis[^42].
Greg Kroah-Hartman said in March: "Something happened a month ago, and the world switched. Now we have real reports." [^43].
Issue #540 asks for GHSA delivery, and Anthropic says it is aiming for that [^2,3].
